rv.q: All in all, here's a trip for retro Broadway fans who like their musicals up close and yet roaring down the track.
Blank Theatre’s ON THE 20TH CENTURY makes for a delightful ride through a farcical facsimile of Broadway’s Silver Age, if one can accommodate a few bumps along the way.
The funkily swinging score has attitude aplenty and could very well hold up to further listening.
If gorgeous, trained singing, high physical comedy and sharp dialogue sound like a good time, you can’t go wrong with this production.
And their newest production, On the Twentieth Century , absolutely shines as it showcases the considerable talents of everyone involved.
Their efforts, however, are essentially wasted by the incredibly confusing and just not funny enough script.
"On the Twentieth Century" is a delightful journey filled with laughter, romance, and sensational musical numbers.

cn.t: Critics praise this rare Chicago revival of the Comden and Green musical as a hilarious, enjoyable romp, though one reviewer questions whether the 1930s farce remains relevant for modern audiences.
